what: Williams owns natural gas pipelines. Its Transco system runs from Texas to New York and is the largest gas pipeline in the United States, carrying roughly a third of the country's natural gas, and it also gathers and processes gas at the wellhead.
customers: Electric utilities and power producers, gas distributors, industrial users and liquefied natural gas export terminals.
money: Transco and Northwest Pipeline capacity sold under long-term contracts
gathering and processing gas in the Marcellus, Utica and western basins
moat: Pipeline rights of way that are effectively impossible to obtain again, and long-term contracts that pay for reserved capacity whether or not gas actually flows.
risks: Debt of about $30 billion is large relative to earnings
New pipeline projects face long permitting fights and legal challenges
Gathering volumes depend on drilling activity it does not control
Rising interest rates raise the cost of refinancing
opportunities: Electricity demand from data centres is driving new gas-fired power plants on its system
Capacity on Transco is contracted years ahead, giving unusually steady cash flow
Liquefied natural gas exports from the Gulf Coast pull more gas through its lines
watch: Newly contracted pipeline expansion projects and the share of earnings coming from fee-based contracts.
